defaults.pdcp_header_required: PDCP mode with Integrity enabled, including Null
defaults.sdap_header: optional; if selected, exactly one byte of Hex is required

protection.integrity: PDCP header || optional SDAP header || plaintext payload
protection.ciphering: Payload || MAC-I; both headers are excluded
protection.input_output: Headers are supplied separately and never included in the payload input/output
protection.receive: When Integrity is enabled, the payload input includes the appended MAC-I, encrypted together with the payload if Ciphering is enabled

coverage: Independent bit-string framing references across algorithms 0-6, SDAP absent/present, aligned/unaligned/empty payloads, legacy and variable MAC lengths.
Changes to actual PDCP/SDAP header values, payload and MAC are detected for non-Null Integrity.
Segments taken from official algorithm messages are reassembled and checked against their fixed official MACs. Such artificial segmentation is not an official PDCP packet vector.
GUI checks cover required headers, SDAP presence, inactive fields, per-tab headers, Raw compatibility, and exact byte/remainder display.
limitations: COUNT remains a manual input; SN/HFN is not inferred or checked against the header.
PDCP header bytes are provided manually; only presence/byte encoding is checked, not bearer format, reserved bits, SN length, or header semantic correctness.
This is an explicit header/payload boundary calculator, not automatic PDU parsing or a complete PDCP/SDAP protocol implementation. NCA remains excluded.
Windows source and EXE were tested on Windows Server 2025 hosted CI. Windows 11 visual/DPI checks were not repeated for this change.
No release tag was published and no merge into main/dev was performed. Existing Markdown documents were left unchanged.
